info.name: sandbox-runner
info.description: sandbox-runner endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/sandbox` → `http://sandbox-runner:8000`, `include_subpath: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/sandbox/ENDPOINTS.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the /v1/sandbox pass-through — most keys created for chat models already do. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.
12-char hex id returned by POST /run. Fill in after spawning to run the /jobs/{id} + DELETE requests.
MCP session id — paste in the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it.

request.description: Liveness + DB status. Returns {"status": "ok", "db": "up"} when the runner can reach sandbox-db; "degraded" / "down" otherwise.

Spawn a static HTML sandbox — nginx serves the files map at /. Returns { sandbox_id, url, expires_at }. The URL uses whatever SANDBOX_PROXY_URL is set to in .env — for browser-reachable iframes, that should be a public URL under the same origin as Open WebUI (e.g. https://chat.zeoenergy.com/sandboxes).

body.raw:
{
  "runtime": "python",
  "files": {
    "app.py": "import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

st.title('sine wave demo')
n = st.slider('samples', 10, 500, 100)
freq = st.slider('frequency', 1, 10, 3)
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': np.sin(freq * x)})
st.line_chart(df.set_index('x'))
"
  },
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}

request.description: Spawn a Streamlit sandbox. Runtime `python` base image has streamlit, gradio, flask, fastapi, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, plotly, requests, pillow pre-installed. Add a requirements.txt to files to install additional deps via sandbox-egress (pypi allowlisted). Cold-start ~2s pre-baked; 20-90s if pip install runs.

Illustrates the install-if-present pattern. If files contains a requirements.txt, the base image entrypoint runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` before executing the command. pip goes through HTTP_PROXY=sandbox-egress:8888 and hits the pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org allowlist.

Spawn a Node sandbox. Base image has serve, vite, react, react-dom, express, next installed globally so `require('express')` works without a package.json. Add a package.json to files to trigger `npm install` on boot.
Multi-file Vite + React counter. Vite HMR uses WebSockets — sandbox-proxy (Caddy) forwards them by default, so buttons work end-to-end when iframed.

List every sandbox in the registry (running + terminal). Fixed limit of 20 in PostgresRegistry.list_all(). Ordered by updated_at DESC. Returns JobsListResponse — see ENDPOINTS.md for the JobBase shape.
Snapshot of one sandbox. 404 if unknown. Set the sandboxId collection variable to the id returned by POST /run first.
Tear a sandbox down early. Stops the container, removes it, deletes the row, releases the concurrency slot. Returns 204 no body. 404 if the sandbox id is unknown.

OpenAPI schema for the OpenWebUI Tool Server integration. Note: OpenWebUI ITSELF should point Admin Panel → Settings → Tools → Add Connection directly at http://sandbox-runner:8000/tool (Docker service DNS on ai_shared), NOT at the LiteLLM pass-through — OpenWebUI needs to see the raw HTMLResponse headers and CORS behavior. Use this Postman request only for schema inspection.

OpenWebUI Rich-UI integration. Returns HTMLResponse with `Content-Disposition: inline` — OpenWebUI renders the response body (an `<iframe>` pointing at sandbox-proxy) as an embedded artifact under the tool call indicator, no model round-trip needed. Response Content-Type is text/html (not JSON). Same warning as /tool/openapi.json — OpenWebUI should register this URL directly on sandbox-runner:8000, not via LiteLLM, so it can see the raw response headers.

item.name: MCP
item.description: FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises the sandbox as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.sandbox` in litellm_config.yaml — models see the tool through that path, not this one. The Postman requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

request.description: MCP handshake. Response headers include `mcp-session-id` — copy it into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable.
Enumerate available tools. sandbox-runner exposes exactly one: preview_app.
Invoke preview_app via MCP. Result body has a text-content block containing a fenced ```html iframe block ready for OpenWebUI's markdown renderer.
Invoke preview_app for a Python (Streamlit) sandbox via MCP.
